conviction_note: A $19bn staple with 17 estimates, 49,624 front-expiry contracts and a company that already reaffirmed its FY2027 guide nine days after this quarter closed offers almost no information asymmetry to a web hunt, and I found no primary-document number that an aggregator does not carry; my findings sum to +0.8 and I emit +0.6, haircut for the +2.75 put skew I am signing against, so the honest content of this hunt is a magnitude claim rather than a direction one — the option market is paying 5.55% on a name whose median reaction over seven prints is 3.06% and whose identical setup a year ago (Q1 FY2026, adjusted EPS -20% cc, organic -3%, full-year outlook reaffirmed) moved the stock -0.77%.
bar: Adjusted diluted EPS $0.72 on net sales $4.35bn, 17 analysts, EPS range $0.68-$0.76 (https://news.alphastreet.com/general-mills-q1-2027-earnings-preview-september-23-street-expects-0-72-eps/amp/, 2026-09-22), corroborated at ~$0.72 / ~$4.35bn by a second preview (https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/stockstory-2026-9-22-general-mills-gis-q3-earnings-what-to-expect, 2026-09-22) and by the sweep row. The company-level bar is the FY2027 guide reaffirmed 2026-09-08: organic net sales -1.5% to +0.5%, adjusted operating profit -13% to -8% cc, adjusted EPS $3.00-$3.20 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260908596763/en/General-Mills-Reaffirms-Annual-Guidance-and-Provides-Business-Update-at-2026-Barclays-Global-Consumer-Staples-Conference). Two agreeing estimate sources plus a company guide, so sizes are not capped on bar uncertainty.
positioning_check: Short interest 46.00m shares = 8.64% of float, 5.60 days to cover, down from 49.10m the prior settlement (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/gis/statistics/, read 2026-09-22, per the sweep row). That is high for a $19bn staple with ~8.9m ADV and it is FALLING, i.e. shorts covering into the print rather than building. Baseline skew_25d = +2.75 vol points, so the option market is explicitly paying up for downside; but front-expiry put/call open interest is 0.55 on 49,624 contracts, a call-heavy outstanding book, so downside is expensive per unit of vol rather than crowded by size. Baseline event-implied move 5.55% against a median realised reaction of 3.06% and a max of 8.53% over seven prints.

findings.finding: General Mills' fiscal Q1 2027 ended 2026-08-30, and on 2026-09-08 — nine days after the quarter closed — the company reaffirmed the full FY2027 guide AND disclosed quarter-specific consumption data (Q1 retail dollar sales +2 points versus Q4, 8 of its top 10 categories gaining dollar share, cereal category dollar sales +2 points, taste-forward cereal brands +5 points, base pound volume from -10% at end-FY2025 to +2% at end-FY2026); so the guidance line this stock actually trades on has already been marked to a completed quarter, and a guidance cut on 2026-09-23 would be a reversal 15 days after a post-close reaffirmation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The closest analogue in the baseline is 2025-09-17 — fiscal Q1 with adjusted EPS -20% in constant currency, organic net sales -3%, gross margin -90bp, and the full-year outlook reaffirmed — which moved the stock -0.77%. The one large positive in the baseline, 2026-07-01 at +8.53%, came from a 17% EPS beat plus a brand-new $3bn savings programme, not from a reaffirmation. And this particular reaffirmation was visibly SOLD: the stock went from $39.26 on 09-03 to $35.96 by 09-10. So the residual value of this finding is only the truncation of the left tail — the market sold it because it wanted a raise, not because it doubts the floor — and it is sized at a fraction of the implied move accordingly.
findings.why_not_priced: Partially priced and I say so. What is not in the price is the TIMING: the wire copy read 'reaffirms guidance at a conference', which the market treats as a mid-quarter statement, and the quarter had in fact already closed. If the market had read it as a post-close pre-announcement, the stock would not have de-rated a further 8% into the print and the front-expiry straddle would not be 1.8x this name's median realised reaction. The specific observable: an implied event move of 5.55% on a name whose guidance range was marked to the completed quarter a fortnight ago.
findings.independence: Fiscal-period convention confirmed by the prior-year Q1 release covering the quarter ended 31 August 2025 (https://investors.generalmills.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/General-Mills-Reports-Fiscal-2026-First-quarter-Results-and-Reaffirms-Full-year-Outlook/default.aspx). The Q1 consumption detail beyond the press-release text comes from a second write-up of the same fireside chat (https://za.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/general-mills-at-barclays-consumer-conference-growth-push-gains-traction-93CH-4456937), so that detail and finding 2 SHARE the 2026-09-08 event as a source and are two readings of one day.

findings.finding: At the same 2026-09-08 fireside chat management said input-cost inflation is tracking toward the HIGH END of the guided 4-5% range with hedge coverage only 6-9 months out (~9 months on crops), while on the 2026-07-01 call it had already said fiscal 2027 profit is weighted to the second half because 'the impact of inflation net of cost savings is expected to be negative in the first quarter' — so the quarter being reported is the one where cost leverage is worst and the $750m of FY2027 savings has not yet phased in.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This lands INSIDE what the company has already guided, which by construction makes it a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, and GIS's own precedent for a bad-margin Q1 with the year reaffirmed is -0.77% (2025-09-17, gross margin 33.9%, down 90bp). The baseline's two largest down reactions, -5.11% (2025-06-25) and -3.06% (2024-12-18), were guidance events rather than pure Q1 margin events. Sized small for that reason.
findings.why_not_priced: The 2026-09-08 press release headline was 'reaffirms annual guidance'; the high-end-of-range inflation detail and the 6-9 month hedge window sat in the fireside chat and not in the release, so it travelled through transcript coverage rather than the wire. If it were fully in the price, the 30-day consensus drift would not have gone UP 1.4% (from $0.71 to $0.72) over exactly the window containing that statement. That said, it is inside a guided range, which is why it is sized below one point.
findings.independence: The first-half cost-savings phasing is independently sourced to the 2026-07-01 earnings call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/01/general-mills-gis-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), a different document and a different date. This finding shares the 2026-09-08 event with finding 1; the two are opposite-signed readings of the same day and are deliberately not double-counted.

findings.finding: The option market is paying an event-implied 5.55% (7.75% front-expiry straddle, 38.3% ATM IV) with a +2.75 put skew on a name whose last seven prints have a median absolute reaction of 3.06% and a maximum of 8.53%, while the short base — 46.0m shares, 8.64% of float, 5.60 days to cover — is already covering from 49.1m, and the entire +8.53% reaction to the 2026-07-01 print has been given back (spot $35.805 against a $40.08 director-grant price on 2026-08-30).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of the baseline's seven reactions were negative, but six of seven were inside 5.55% and five of seven were inside 3.5%. The one time this name exceeded the currently-implied move was 2026-07-01, which required a 17% EPS beat plus a new multi-year savings programme. Nothing of that class is on the table on 2026-09-23.
findings.why_not_priced: I am signing against the skew, so I have to say why the option market is wrong about THIS print: the downside being bought is dividend-cut and structural-derating contagion — Campbell's cut its dividend 36% on 2026-09-03 and GIS fell 3.25% the same day, and GIS now yields ~6.8% — but a dividend cut is not an event this print can deliver. GIS declared its $0.61 quarterly dividend with the 2026-07-01 release (paid 2026-08-03) and the next board declaration sits with the late-September annual-meeting cycle, ex-date 2026-10-12, outside the window. If the skew were about the quarter rather than about the payout and the sector, the put/call open-interest ratio would not be 0.55. The counterweight is real and is why this is sized at 0.7 rather than 2: the resolved record has a hunter losing 11 points to a large put skew, and a covering short base is a reason to shrink a negative, not a licence to enlarge a positive.
findings.independence: The Campbell's dividend cut and the same-day GIS move are sourced separately (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/03/campbells-slides-9-36-dividend-cut-general-mills-falls-4-kraft-heinz-drops-3/, 2026-09-03). The implied-move and skew numbers come from the sealed baseline, not from this URL. Cutting the other way, and recorded rather than buried: the 2026-09-08 reaffirmation was met with an ~8% five-session decline (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Why+General+Mills+(GIS)+Stock+Is+Down+Today, 2026-09-10), which is evidence the marginal holder is selling regardless of the guide.

outside_window.finding: General Mills is a PLAINTIFF, with Mars, Kellanova and McKee Foods, in an antitrust suit filed 2026-09-04 in federal court in Chicago alleging US sugar producers fixed granulated sugar prices from January 2017 to at least October 2024 — a gain contingency, not a liability, that no preview treats as an asset and that cannot resolve on 2026-09-23.

The Brazil business (Yoki, Kitano) was sold to 3coracoes for a R$800m base price and CLOSED on 2026-09-03, which is fiscal Q2 2027 and not the quarter being reported; the $1,032m non-cash pre-tax held-for-sale valuation loss was already taken in Q4 FY2026, so any final close adjustment and CTA recycling lands in the December print.

The next quarterly dividend declaration falls with the late-September board/annual-meeting cycle, ex-date 2026-10-12, payable 2026-11-03 — so the payout question the 6.8% yield is pricing is not settled by this print.

searched_and_found_nothing: A Pet/Blue Buffalo negative worth filing: GIS's own 2026-09-08 line that Blue Buffalo Wilderness 'may take 18 months to 2 years to return to growth' plus the guided low-single-digit FY27 retail-inventory headwind is pre-guided, Pet is only ~14% of sales ($610m of $4.52bn in the year-ago quarter) against a North America Retail segment management says gained share in 8 of its top 10 categories, and the independent read cuts the other way — Chewy on 2026-09-09 said the pet market 'did not meaningfully recover... but also did not deteriorate further' and RAISED its FY outlook (https://investor.chewy.com/news-and-events/news/news-details/2026/Chewy-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx). Net of the rest of the company this is not a finding, so it is not one.

A 'low bar on seasonality' argument: $0.72 is 23.2% of the $3.10 FY27 midpoint against $0.86 / ~$3.60 = 23.9% for the prior year. The bar is normal for a GIS Q1, not conspicuously low, so I dropped this line rather than sizing it.

Insider signal: all Form 4s since 2026-06-01 are routine — non-employee director retainer shares issued 2026-05-31 at $33.65 and 2026-08-30 at $40.08 under the 2022 Stock Compensation Plan (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040704/000162828026059544/wk-form4_1788200689.xml). No open-market cluster.
Quiet 8-K: EDGAR shows NO 8-K filed by CIK 0000040704 since the 2026-07-01 results 8-K; the 2026-09-08 reaffirmation was a press release only. Nothing hidden in the filing record.
Bernstein's Underperform on GIS/CPB/CAG/KHC turned out to be dated JUNE 2026, not September, despite September-looking search framing — checked and discarded as a driver of the current drawdown.

A causal, company-specific explanation for the -12.5% 20-day run-up beyond sector de-rating, the Campbell's dividend cut on 09-03, a JPMorgan Sell reiteration and an Evercore target trim to $38 on 09-14: there isn't one, and an unexplained drawdown on a 17-analyst mega-cap is not evidence of over-reaction.

Free September Circana/Nielsen takeaway data for cereal or pet that post-dates the company's own 2026-09-08 disclosure — Circana's pet release would not render and nothing else is public at that granularity.
A quantified Q1 FY2027 figure in any primary document not already carried by the wire. There is none; this is a mega-cap with full coverage, which is the reason every size here is small.
baseline_tension: My net sign cuts AGAINST the baseline: the +2.75 put skew and the -12.5% 20-day run-up both say down and I am emitting a small positive, justified only by the guide having been marked to a completed quarter on 2026-09-08 and by an implied 5.55% that is 1.8x this name's median 3.06% reaction — which is why the emitted number is well below the implied move and below the sum of the findings.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number): my draft had expected_move_pct equal to the finding sum while baseline_tension said I cut against the skew and the run-up. Emitted move is now +0.6 against a finding sum of +0.8, and conviction_note says by how much and why.

Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat): my draft noted the +2.75 skew and went long anyway without saying why the option market is wrong about THIS print. The positioning finding is cut from +1.2 to +0.7 and now carries the explicit reason — the puts are hedging dividend-cut/sector contagion after Campbell's 36% cut on 09-03, and the dividend declaration is outside this window.

Lesson 6 (a finding inside the guided range is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): the inflation finding is inside the company's own guided 4-5% range and inside its stated Q1 negative-leverage phasing, so it was cut from -1.0 to -0.7 and its why_not_priced now says so.

Lesson 8, read in inverse (thin coverage means a confirmed fact moves more): GIS is a 17-estimate, 49,624-contract mega-cap, so the understatement warning does not apply here and the opposite does — every size stayed small and print_vs_bar_pct came down from +4.0 to +3.5.

Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest of the company): the Pet/Blue Buffalo negative I had been circling was dropped entirely rather than filed, because Pet is ~14% of sales against a North America Retail segment gaining share in 8 of its top 10 categories, and Chewy's 09-09 print contradicts it. It is recorded in searched_and_found_nothing.

'What has worked' (documents beat inference): I have no primary-document number an aggregator does not carry, and the file says that is the only class of finding that has paid. That is the main reason the emitted number is +0.6 and not larger.
'The date is on the URL path': the Bernstein Underperform on GIS was served as a September story and the underlying URLs date it to early June 2026. Discarded as a current driver.
